mainTopic: The ברכות of the כהנים in the מקדש, why עשרת הדברות were removed from daily prayer, whether a ברכה follows its start or its ending, and רב's rulings on אמת ויציב and bowing in תפילה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an argument from the previous amud: which single ברכה did the כהנים in the מקדש say before קריאת שמע? ריש לקיש's rule that 'the ברכות do not hold each other back' seems to prove it was יוצר אור. But the גמרא shows this was only an inference, and the rule could just mean the order of the ברכות does not matter. Next, the גמרא returns to the משנה in תמיד. The כהנים read עשרת הדברות daily, but this was cancelled everywhere else because of the complaint of the מינים, and later חכמים were not allowed to bring it back. It also gives the words of the שבת blessing the outgoing משמר gave the incoming one. Then the גמרא asks about a ברכה that starts with the wrong food in mind and ends with the right one: do we follow the start or the ending? Every proof it brings from a ברייתא is pushed aside, so the question is never settled. The amud ends with rulings of רב: say אמת ויציב in the morning and אמת ואמונה at night, and in תפילה bow at ברוך and straighten up at God's name.

steps.title: Finishing the inference: the blessing must have been יוצר אור
steps.stepSummary: If the כהנים had said only אהבה רבה, there would be no proof that one ברכה does not hold back the other. So the ברכה they said must have been יוצר אור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say they were saying 'אהבה רבה', how could we learn that the ברכות do not hold each other back? Maybe they skipped 'יוצר אור' only because its time had not come yet, and once its time came they did say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the line of reasoning that led to the conclusion that the כהנים said יוצר אור. It shows why the other option, אהבה רבה, cannot work with ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's rule that 'ברכות אין מעכבות' needs a case where one ברכה was skipped completely. If the כהנים skipped אהבה רבה, that is a real skip. If they skipped יוצר אור, it could simply be that it was too early: יוצר אור praises the creation of the sunlight, and the כהנים said their ברכות before sunrise. So only the option of 'they said יוצר אור' proves ריש לקיש's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Abounding love', the second ברכה before קריאת שמע
'Who creates light', the first morning ברכה before קריאת שמע

keyTerms.term: בְּרָכוֹת אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: The ברכות do not hold each other back; missing one does not cancel the other

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT a new question. It is the second half of an argument that started on the previous amud ('if you say יוצר אור, fine... but if you say אהבה רבה...'). Read it as the end of a proof.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אִי אָמְרַתְּ ״אַהֲבָה רַבָּה״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי,
phrases.english: But if you say they were saying 'Abounding love',

phrases.aramaic: מַאי בְּרָכוֹת אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ?
phrases.english: how do we know that the blessings do not hold each other back?
phrases.notes: The word מאי here means: from where could we learn this?

phrases.english: Perhaps the fact that they did not say 'Who creates light'
was because the time for 'Who creates light' had not yet come,
phrases.notes: The כהנים said their ברכות very early, before sunrise.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מְטָא זְמַן ״יוֹצֵר אוֹר״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי.
phrases.english: and when the time for 'Who creates light' came, they would say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִי אָמְרַתְּ ״אַהֲבָה רַבָּה״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'if you say X... but if you say Y...' inference begun on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That the one ברכה the כהנים said was יוצר אור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's rule that ברכות אין מעכבות זו את זו, which can only be proven if the skipped ברכה was אהבה רבה.

steps.title: Why does it matter that this was only an inference?
steps.stepSummary: The inference seems solid, so the גמרא asks what difference it makes that the answer came from inference and not from an open statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was learned by inference, so what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: the reasoning looks convincing, so why stress that it was 'only' an inference? This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, someone said the teaching was not stated outright but learned מכללא, by inference. Since the proof in Step 1 seems tight, the גמרא wants to know what weakness an inference has here.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; worked out from a general statement rather than said openly
What? (here: so what? what difference does it make?)

phrases.english: And if it is by inference, what of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how much weight to give the 'it was only an inference' report, given the strong proof in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical weakness comes from the conclusion being based on inference rather than an open statement?

steps.title: An inference can be explained away: the rule may be about order
steps.stepSummary: Since it is only an inference, we can say the כהנים said אהבה רבה first and יוצר אור later. ריש לקיש's rule would then mean only that the ORDER of the ברכות does not hold one back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it is only an inference, you could say: really they said 'אהבה רבה', and when the time for 'יוצר אור' came they said that too. And what does 'the ברכות do not hold each other back' mean? It means the order of the ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that an inference is weaker because it can be read another way. It gives that other reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 assumed ריש לקיש meant that a person may skip one ברכה completely. But his words could just mean that saying the ברכות in the wrong order does not stop you from fulfilling your obligation. The כהנים did exactly that: אהבה רבה first, יוצר אור after sunrise. On this reading, ריש לקיש's rule tells us nothing about which single ברכה the כהנים said, so the 'proof' for יוצר אור falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (introduces the actual reading)

steps.whatToRemember: Because the answer 'יוצר אור' was only an inference, it is not certain. ריש לקיש's rule can be read as being only about the ORDER of the ברכות, so it does not prove which ברכה the כהנים said.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two meanings of 'ברכות אין מעכבות' apart: (1) you may skip one ברכה entirely, or (2) you may say them out of order. Step 1 relied on meaning 1. Step 3 switches to meaning 2.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a conclusion reached by inference (מכללא) is weaker than an open statement, because the source can be read another way.

phrases.english: For if it is by inference,
really they were saying 'Abounding love',

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מְטָא זְמַן ״יוֹצֵר אוֹר״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and when the time for 'Who creates light' came, they would say it.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי ״בְּרָכוֹת אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ״
phrases.english: And what is meant by 'the blessings do not hold each other back'?
The order of the blessings.
phrases.notes: Saying them out of order does not stop you from fulfilling the obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי מִכְּלָלָא, לְעוֹלָם ״אַהֲבָה רַבָּה״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 2 by showing how the inference of Step 1 can be undone.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An inference can be read differently: the כהנים may have said אהבה רבה and later יוצר אור, and ריש לקיש's rule refers only to the order of the ברכות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from ריש לקיש's rule that the single ברכה was יוצר אור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed 'אין מעכבות' means skipping a ברכה completely, when it could mean only that the order does not matter.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: what the כהנים read in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the כהנים read עשרת הדברות, שמע, והיה אם שמוע, ויאמר, אמת ויציב, עבודה, and ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they read the עשרת הדברות, שמע, והיה אם שמוע, ויאמר, אמת ויציב, עבודה, and ברכת כהנים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברכה discussion is finished, so the גמרא goes back and quotes the next line of the משנה about the daily service of the כהנים. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line lists everything the כהנים read in the מקדש each morning. Most notable is that עשרת הדברות was read along with the parts of קריאת שמע. The גמרא repeats the line here so it can discuss it, especially the reading of עשרת הדברות.

keyTerms.meaning: The third paragraph of שמע (the section about ציצית)
'True and firm', the ברכה said after the morning שמע
The ברכה about the Temple service (רצה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next topic: why עשרת הדברות was read in the מקדש but was not added to קריאת שמע outside it.

phrases.english: And they read the Ten Commandments,
'Hear', 'And it shall be if you listen', 'And He said',
'True and firm', the Temple service blessing, and the Priestly Blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the ברכה discussion, the גמרא returns to quoting the משנה to analyze its next clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים in the מקדש read עשרת הדברות, the three paragraphs of שמע, אמת ויציב, עבודה, and ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: Outside the Temple they also wanted to say the Ten Commandments
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says that people wanted to read עשרת הדברות daily in the גבולין too, but this was stopped because of the complaint of the מינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Even outside the מקדש, people wanted to read this way. But it had already been cancelled because of the complaint of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new teaching to the משנה we just quoted. It explains why only the כהנים in the מקדש read עשרת הדברות, and not everyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה described the daily order in the מקדש, which included עשרת הדברות. שמואל says people outside wanted to copy this, but the רבנן stopped it. The reason was the מינים, who claimed only עשרת הדברות came from הקב"ה. Saying them every day would look like support for that claim.
steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that עשרת הדברות are bad to say. The fear is that saying ONLY them every day would look like the rest of the תורה is less important, which is exactly what the מינים claimed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why עשרת הדברות are not part of our daily קריאת שמע and תפילה today.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Even in the outlying areas they wanted to read this way,
phrases.notes: "This way" means including the Ten Commandments, like the כהנים in the מקדש.

phrases.english: but they had already cancelled them
because of the complaint of the heretics.
phrases.notes: The heretics claimed only the Ten Commandments were given by G-d.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new teaching about the עשרת הדברות part of the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading עשרת הדברות every day outside the מקדש was cancelled because of the complaint of the מינים.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי נתן says the same thing as שמואל, which supports his teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. רבי נתן says: Outside the מקדש they wanted to read this way, but it had already been cancelled because of the complaint of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as שמואל. This gives support to what שמואל said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "תניא נמי הכי" means an older source, from the time of the תנאים, agrees. רבי נתן uses almost the exact same words. So שמואל's teaching is not just his own idea; it matches a תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports this)
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: It was also taught this way in a baraita:
Rabbi Natan says:
In the outlying areas they wanted to read this way,
but they had already cancelled them
because of the complaint of the heretics.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's statement from step 5 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's statement that the daily reading of עשרת הדברות in the גבולין was cancelled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי נתן with the same wording.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה wanted to bring it back in סורא
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה wanted to set up the daily reading of עשרת הדברות in סורא, but רב חסדא told him it was already cancelled because of the מינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה thought to set it up in סורא. רב חסדא said to him: They already cancelled it because of the complaint of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. A great אמורא tried to bring back the daily reading of עשרת הדברות, and he was stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe רבה בר בר חנה thought the worry about the מינים did not apply in his place or time. רב חסדא answers that the cancellation still stands. A תקנה made by the רבנן is not undone just because one place wants it.

keyTerms.meaning: To set them up as a fixed practice
A major תורה city in בבל

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה סְבַר לְמִקְבְּעִינְהוּ בְּסוּרָא,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana thought to set them up in Sura,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the daily reading of the Ten Commandments.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him:
They already cancelled them because of the complaint of the heretics.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה סְבַר לְמִקְבְּעִינְהוּ בְּסוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule from steps 5 and 6 being applied in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a great אמורא may not bring back the daily reading of עשרת הדברות, since it was already cancelled.

steps.title: אמימר wanted to bring it back in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: אמימר wanted to set up the daily reading of עשרת הדברות in נהרדעא, but רב אשי told him the same thing: it was already cancelled because of the מינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר thought to set it up in נהרדעא. רב אשי said to him: They already cancelled it because of the complaint of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, later story with the same ending. This closes the topic: the cancellation stays in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This happens generations after the first story, near the end of the תלמוד. Again a great חכם wants to bring the practice back, and again he is stopped with the same words. The repetition shows the rule is firm and does not fade over time.

keyTerms.meaning: A major תורה city in בבל
The leading אמורא of his generation, editor of the תלמוד

steps.whatToRemember: The כהנים in the מקדש read עשרת הדברות every day. Everyone wanted to do this outside too, but the רבנן cancelled it because of the מינים, who claimed only עשרת הדברות came from הקב"ה. Even great אמוראים in later generations were not allowed to bring it back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why our daily davening does not include עשרת הדברות, even though they are central to the תורה.

phrases.english: Ameimar thought to set them up in Nehardea,
Rav Ashi said to him:
They already cancelled them because of the complaint of the heretics.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story, parallel to step 7, that confirms the rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The daily reading of עשרת הדברות outside the מקדש stays cancelled for all generations because of the complaint of the מינים.

steps.title: On שבת an extra ברכה is added for the outgoing משמר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה from תמיד: on שבת, one extra blessing is added for the outgoing משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on שבת, they add one blessing for the outgoing משמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the משנה about what the כהנים did in the בית המקדש. This line sets up a question about what the extra blessing was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים were split into groups called משמרות, and each group served for one week. The groups switched on שבת, so on that day one group left and a new group came in. The משנה says one extra blessing was added for that changeover.

keyTerms.meaning: A priestly watch, one of the groups of כהנים that took turns serving in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And on Shabbat they add one blessing
phrases.notes: Continues the משנה from תמיד quoted in Step 4

phrases.english: for the outgoing priestly watch.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְשַׁבָּת מוֹסִיפִין בְּרָכָה אַחַת לַמִּשְׁמָר הַיּוֹצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the discussion of reading עשרת הדברות to the next line of the משנה in תמיד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, one extra blessing is said for the outgoing משמר.

steps.title: What is the one extra blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words of this extra blessing were.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'one blessing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: the משנה mentions a blessing, so what did it actually say?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the משנה. The משנה just does not tell us the words of the blessing, so the גמרא wants that information.

phrases.english: What is the 'one blessing'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of the blessing mentioned in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual words of the extra שבת blessing.

steps.title: רבי חלבו gives the words of the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו says the outgoing משמר blessed the incoming משמר that the One Who rests His Name in this house should bring love, brotherhood, peace and friendship among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said: The outgoing משמר says to the incoming משמר: 'May He Who caused His Name to dwell in this House cause love, brotherhood, peace and friendship to dwell among you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלבו answers the question by giving the exact words the leaving group said to the new group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing was not about the עבודה itself. It was a wish for unity and peace among the new group of כהנים. They were serving together in God's house, so the blessing asks that God's presence bring harmony among them.

keyTerms.meaning: The one coming in (the incoming group)

steps.whatToRemember: The משמר changeover on שבת included a blessing of love and peace from the outgoing כהנים to the incoming ones.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said:
The outgoing watch says to the incoming watch:
"He Who caused His Name to dwell in this House,
may He cause to dwell among you
love and brotherhood, peace and friendship."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing is: מי ששכן את שמו בבית הזה הוא ישכין ביניכם אהבה ואחוה ושלום וריעות.

steps.title: Back to our משנה: where they said to make it long
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to a line from our own משנה: מקום שאמרו להאריך, where the חכמים said to make a ברכה long, one may not shorten it.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We learned in the משנה:] 'Where they said to make it long...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה in ברכות and quotes the rule about not changing the form of a ברכה. This line sets up a new discussion about a ברכה that starts one way and ends another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that the form of a ברכה set by the חכמים, long or short, may not be changed. People learned from this that the ending (חתימה) of a ברכה matters a lot. The גמרא now uses this idea to ask about a ברכה whose start and ending don't match.

keyTerms.meaning: To make long (a long ברכה with an ending)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not about the כהנים anymore. The גמרא has switched back to our own משנה in ברכות, about the ברכות of קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: Where they said to make it long.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה on 11a: one may not shorten a long ברכה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the משנה in תמיד and starts a new topic from our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברכה set by the חכמים as long may not be shortened. This sets up the question of which part of a ברכה counts.

steps.title: The obvious case: wine thought to be beer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious that someone holding wine who thought it was beer, began the ברכה with beer in mind, and ended with the wine ending is יוצא. Even saying שהכל would have worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that where one holds a cup of wine in his hand, thinks it is beer, begins the blessing with beer in mind, and ends with the wine ending, he has fulfilled his obligation. Because even if he had said 'שהכל נהיה בדברו', he would have fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: Before asking the real question, the גמרא first clears away an easy case that has a clear answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case, both halves of the ברכה are valid for wine. He started with שהכל in mind, and שהכל works for any food or drink בדיעבד. He ended with בורא פרי הגפן, which is the exact ברכה for wine. Since nothing he did was wrong for wine, it does not matter whether we follow the start or the end.

keyTerms.meaning: With the intention of, having in mind

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Here the cup really is WINE, so both parts of the ברכה fit. The hard case in Step 15 is the reverse: the cup is really beer.

phrases.english: It is obvious: where one is holding
a cup of wine in his hand
and he thinks that it is beer,
and he began and blesses with beer in mind,
phrases.notes: He meant to say שהכל

phrases.english: and he ended with the wine ending, he fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: He ended with בורא פרי הגפן

phrases.english: For even if he had said
'By Whose word all things came to be', he would have fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא הֵיכָא דְּקָא נָקֵיט כָּסָא דְחַמְרָא בִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clears away a simple case so the real question can be asked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine thought to be beer: if he started with שהכל in mind and ended with בורא פרי הגפן, he is יוצא, because both parts are valid for wine.

steps.title: Source: שהכל works for everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה as the source that saying שהכל on any food is valid בדיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we learned in a משנה: On all of them, if he said 'שהכל נהיה בדברו', he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claim in Step 13 that שהכל works for wine by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (ברכות 40a) says that שהכל works בדיעבד for all foods, even ones that have their own special ברכה. So the beer-intended start was not a mistake for wine, and the case in Step 13 is truly obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: For we learned in a משנה
'By Whose word all things came to be', the general ברכה

phrases.english: For we learned in a Mishnah:
On all of them, if he said
'By Whose word all things came to be', he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reasoning of Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that שהכל is valid on wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ברכות 40a: על כולם אם אמר שהכל נהיה בדברו יצא.

steps.title: The real question: beer thought to be wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the reverse case: someone holding beer thinks it is wine, starts the ברכה with wine in mind, and ends with the beer ending (שהכל). What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: But where one holds a cup of beer in his hand and thinks it is wine, begins the blessing with wine in mind, and ends with the beer ending, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the real question, which is the opposite case from Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the start of the ברכה was meant as בורא פרי הגפן, and that does NOT work for beer. The ending, שהכל, is correct for beer. So one part is wrong and one part is right, and the answer is not obvious.

phrases.english: But where one is holding
a cup of beer in his hand
and he thinks that it is wine,
he began and blessed with wine in mind,
and he ended with the beer ending, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּקָא נָקֵיט כָּסָא דְשִׁכְרָא בִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the obvious case to the reverse case, which is a real question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is someone יוצא if his ברכה over beer began with wine in mind but ended with שהכל?

steps.title: Do we follow the start of the blessing or its ending?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the two sides of the question: do we judge the ברכה by its main beginning or by its closing ending?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we go after the main part of the blessing, or do we go after the ending?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why Step 15 is a real question by laying out the two possible ways to look at it. The next steps try to prove an answer from sources, but each proof is pushed away and the question is never resolved (see Step 26).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the main start of the ברכה (עיקר ברכה) decides, he is not יוצא, because he started with wine in mind. If the ending (חתימה) decides, he is יוצא, because he ended with שהכל. This links back to the idea from our משנה that the חתימה is an important part of a ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The main part of the blessing (its beginning)
The closing ending of a blessing

steps.whatToRemember: The question: when the start of a ברכה and its ending do not match, which one decides, the עיקר ברכה or the חתימה?
steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides how we think about any ברכה said with a mistake partway through: is it judged by how it started or by how it ended?

phrases.english: Do we follow the main part of the blessing,
or do we follow the ending?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question asked in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a ברכה is judged by its עיקר (beginning) or by its חתימה (ending).

steps.title: A ברייתא about mixing up the morning and evening ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. In both שחרית and ערבית, a person who ends with the wrong ending is not יוצא, and a person who ends with the right ending is יוצא, even if he began wrongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: In the morning, if he began with 'Who creates light' and ended with 'Who brings on evenings', he did not fulfill his obligation. If he began with 'Who brings on evenings' and ended with 'Who creates light', he fulfilled it. In the evening, if he began with 'Who brings on evenings' and ended with 'Who creates light', he did not fulfill it. If he began with 'Who creates light' and ended with 'Who brings on evenings', he fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question from Step 16. It describes people who mixed up the morning ברכה (יוצר אור) and the evening ברכה (מעריב ערבים).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all four cases, the person is יוצא only when the ending matches the time of day. The beginning does not matter. This is the same pattern as our beer and wine question, where the beginning was wrong and the ending was acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This phrase introduces a proof from a source.
'Who creates light', the morning ברכה before שמע
'Who brings on evenings', the evening ברכה before שמע
Did not fulfill / did fulfill his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get lost in the four cases. There is one simple pattern: whichever ending he says decides whether he is יוצא. A correct beginning with a wrong ending fails. A wrong beginning with a correct ending works.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: Introduces a proof from a ברייתא

phrases.english: In the morning prayer, if he began with 'Who creates light'
phrases.notes: This is the correct opening for the morning

phrases.english: and ended with 'Who brings on evenings', he did not fulfill his obligation.
phrases.notes: The ending is wrong, so he is not יוצא

phrases.english: If he began with 'Who brings on evenings'
phrases.notes: This is the wrong opening for the morning

phrases.english: and ended with 'Who creates light', he fulfilled it.
phrases.notes: The ending is right, so he is יוצא

phrases.english: In the evening prayer, if he began with 'Who brings on evenings'
phrases.notes: This is the correct opening for the evening

phrases.english: and ended with 'Who creates light', he did not fulfill it.
phrases.notes: The ending is wrong

phrases.english: If he began with 'Who creates light'
phrases.notes: This is the wrong opening for the evening

phrases.english: and ended with 'Who brings on evenings', he fulfilled it.
phrases.notes: The ending is right

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שַׁחֲרִית, פָּתַח בְּ״יוֹצֵר אוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to answer the question in Step 16: do we follow the beginning or the end?
steps.raayaObject: That a ברכה is judged by its closing, so the beer case (wrong start, שהכל ending) would be valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the ברכות before קריאת שמע in שחרית and ערבית

steps.title: The ברייתא's general rule: everything follows the closing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sums up its cases with a general rule: הכל הולך אחר החתום, everything follows the closing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The general principle is: everything follows the closing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states the rule behind its four cases. This rule is the heart of the proof the גמרא wants to use for the beer and wine question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is worded as a broad principle, not just a rule for שמע. If it applies to every ברכה, then in the beer case the שהכל ending would decide, and the person would be יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: The general principle of the matter
Everything follows the closing of the ברכה
The closing or ending of a ברכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is widely used in the הלכות of ברכות. The next step shows that the גמרא limits how far it reaches.

phrases.english: The general principle is:
phrases.notes: Introduces the summary rule

phrases.english: Everything follows the closing.
phrases.notes: This seems to answer the question in Step 16

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָלוֹ שֶׁל דָּבָר: הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַחִתּוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by stating the general principle behind its cases
steps.raayaObject: That every ברכה is decided by its closing

steps.title: The proof is rejected: long ברכות have their own closing with ברוך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברכות of שמע are different, because their closing is a separate line that starts with ברוך (ברוך יוצר המאורות). A short food ברכה has nothing like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because he says 'Blessed is He Who forms the lights'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the ברייתא. It shows that the ברכות of שמע are a different kind of ברכה from a food ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוצר אור and מעריב ערבים are long ברכות. They end with a separate closing line that begins with ברוך, so that closing can stand on its own as a full ברכה. A short ברכה like בורא פרי הגפן or שהכל has no separate closing. So we cannot assume the ending 'fixes' a wrong beginning, and the question from Step 16 stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. A standard phrase for rejecting a proof.
'Who forms the lights', the closing line of the morning ברכה
'Blessed', the word that opens a ברכה's closing line
A long ברכה that has a separate closing

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא teaches הכל הולך אחר החתום for long ברכות that have their own ברוך closing. It does not prove the rule for short food ברכות, so the beer and wine question is still unanswered.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the rule הכל הולך אחר החתום is wrong. It is only saying the rule may apply to long ברכות and not to short ones.

phrases.english: It is different there
phrases.notes: There = the ברכות of שמע in the ברייתא

phrases.english: because he says 'Blessed is He Who forms the lights'.
phrases.notes: The closing is its own line starting with ברוך

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא in Steps 17 and 18
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The ברייתא's rule still stands for long ברכות, and the question from Step 16 remains open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא deals with long ברכות whose closing is a separate ברוך line that can stand alone. Short food ברכות have no such closing, so the comparison does not hold.

steps.title: The closing line has no mention of God as King
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the distinction from step 19. It works for רב, but according to רבי יוחנן the closing line ברוך יוצר המאורות is not a full ברכה, because it has no מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רב, who said: any ברכה without mention of God's name is not a ברכה. The closing line has God's name, so it is fine. But according to רבי יוחנן, who said: any ברכה without mention of God's kingship is not a ברכה, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason it just gave for why the ברכות of שמע are different from food ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the closing line of the ברכות of שמע counts as its own separate ברכה. That works if a ברכה only needs God's name (רב). But רבי יוחנן says a ברכה also needs מלכות ("מלך העולם"), and the closing line does not say that, so for him it is not a separate ברכה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out fine (according to one view)
What is there to say? (a challenge formula)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new attack on the main question. The target is the answer from step 19, which said the ברכות of שמע are special because their closing is a separate ברכה.

phrases.english: This works well for Rav, who said

phrases.aramaic: כָּל בְּרָכָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ הַזְכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם
phrases.english: any blessing that has no mention of God's name
is not a blessing; that is fine.
phrases.notes: The closing ברוך אתה ה' יוצר המאורות does include God's name.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said
any blessing that has no mention of God's kingship
is not a blessing,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דחיה of step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ברוך יוצר המאורות is a separate, complete ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי יוחנן, a ברכה without מלכות is not a ברכה. The closing line lacks מלכות, so it cannot count as an independent ברכה, and the distinction from food ברכות falls away.

steps.title: The opening of the ברכה fits both day and night
steps.stepSummary: Using רבה בר עולא, the גמרא explains that the opening of the ברכות of שמע already mentions both day and night. So its opening, with God's name and kingship, was never really wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since רבה בר עולא said that we mention day at night and night in the day, when a person says the ברכה with מלכות at the beginning, he is saying it about both day and night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason why the ברכות of שמע are different from food ברכות. This reason works even for רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר עולא taught that the morning ברכה mentions night ("ובורא חושך") and the evening ברכה mentions day ("גולל אור"). So the opening, with God's name and kingship, fits both times, and a person who started with the "wrong" one did not really start wrongly. That is why the ending decides there, and this proves nothing about a food ברכה whose opening truly was wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose teaching is used here
The theme of day, mentioned at night
On both of them (day and night)

steps.whyThisMatters: The proof from the ברייתא is still blocked, but now for a different reason. The point is no longer that the closing is a separate ברכה. The point is that the opening was never truly wrong.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא:
phrases.english: Rather, since Rabba bar Ulla said:
in order to mention the theme of day at night
and the theme of night in the day,
when he says God's name and kingship at the beginning
he is saying it about both.
phrases.notes: So the opening was never really a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinguishing reason (replaces the reason from step 19)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברכות of שמע are different only because the closing is a separate ברכה, which fails according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברכות of שמע are different because their opening, with מלכות, covers both day and night, so the opening is never truly wrong.

steps.title: Proof from the words "the general rule"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again with the ברייתא's general rule. The extra words "the general rule" should add something, so perhaps they add our case of short food ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the end of the ברייתא: "The general rule is: everything follows the closing." What does "the general rule" come to include? Doesn't it include the case we were discussing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof that a ברכה follows its closing, even a short food ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a ברייתא says כללו של דבר, "the general rule," it usually means to include more cases beyond the ones it listed. The גמרא suggests that the extra case here is ours: short ברכות like the ones on wine and beer.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a source
The general rule of the matter

phrases.english: Come and hear from the latter clause:
"The general rule is:
everything follows the closing."
"The general rule" comes to include what?
Doesn't it come to include what we said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a second proof from the same ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That a short food ברכה also follows its closing
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words כללו של דבר in the ברייתא

steps.title: The rule includes bread and dates instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The general rule comes to include a case of bread and dates, not wine and beer.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It comes to include a case of bread and dates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the proof by giving the extra words a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words כללו של דבר do add a case, but that case is bread and dates. So they tell us nothing about our wine-and-beer question.

phrases.english: No, it comes to include bread and dates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only this reading of כללו של דבר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra words can refer to a different case (bread and dates), so they are not proof for our question.

steps.title: The simple bread-and-dates case is just our question again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the bread-and-dates case is. If it means someone opened with dates in mind and ended with the bread ending, that is identical to our unanswered question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he ate bread, thought he ate dates, began the ברכה with dates in mind, and ended with the bread ending, that is exactly our question!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer from step 23 by asking what the bread-and-dates case looks like. It shows that the most obvious version does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bread-and-dates case is "started for one food, ended for the other," it is the same as the wine-and-beer case. Then the ברייתא would be answering our question after all, and the דחיה would collapse. So the גמרא must find a different version of the bread-and-dates case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?
If you say (the first suggestion, about to be rejected)
With the thought of, having in mind

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not concluding anything here. It knocks out the obvious version of the bread-and-dates case and is setting up a different explanation that comes next.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that he ate bread,
and thought that he ate dates,
and began the blessing with dates in mind
and ended with the bread ending,
that is exactly our question!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דחיה of step 23 by asking what its case looks like
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 23 that כללו של דבר includes bread and dates rather than our case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The simplest bread-and-dates case (opened for dates, closed for bread) is the same as wine-and-beer. If the ברייתא rules on it, it answers our question, so the דחיה fails unless a different case is meant.

steps.title: The bread-and-dates case is a special situation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the general rule covers someone who ate dates, thought they were bread, opened with the bread ברכה, and ended with the dates ending. He is יוצא, but only because even a bread ending would have worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the rule is needed for this case: a person ate dates but thought he ate bread. He began the ברכה with the bread wording and finished it with the dates wording. He is יוצא, because even if he had finished with the bread wording, he would also be יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24. It shows that the bread-and-dates case is different from our unanswered question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the bread opening is not truly wrong for dates, since he would be יוצא even with a full bread ברכה. So the case says nothing about an opening that is truly wrong. This follows the same pattern as step 21, where the opening turned out to be acceptable after all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a specific case)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this case proves that a wrong opening with a right ending works. Here the opening was never really wrong, because a bread ברכה is acceptable for dates after the fact.

phrases.english: No, it is only needed:
for a case where he ate dates,
and he thought he ate bread,
and he opened with the wording for bread,
and he concluded with the wording for dates; he fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: The bracketed word is part of the printed text.

phrases.english: For even if he had concluded with the wording for bread,
he would also have fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24's challenge by defining the bread-and-dates case so that it differs from the unresolved question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) so that the opening is not truly wrong
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bread-and-dates case seemed identical to our question: a wrong opening with a right ending.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here even the bread opening and ending would work for dates, so the case does not address a truly wrong opening.

steps.title: Why a bread blessing works for dates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a bread ברכה would work for dates. It answers that dates also give a person nourishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because dates also nourish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind step 25. A bread ברכה works for dates because dates are also filling and nourishing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since dates nourish, a ברכה about God feeding us fits them, at least after the fact. This is what makes the bread opening acceptable. As a result, the original question about a truly wrong opening with a right ending remains unresolved.
steps.whatToRemember: The search for a source has ended without an answer. Every proof brought turned out to involve an opening that was not truly wrong. So the question of a wrong opening with a right ending stays open.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because dates also nourish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind step 25's claim that a bread ending would also work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would someone be יוצא for dates with a bread ברכה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dates are also nourishing, so the bread ברכה fits them after the fact.

steps.title: Saying אמת ויציב in the morning and אמת ואמונה at night
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חיננא סבא says in the name of רב that if one does not say אמת ויציב in שחרית and אמת ואמונה in ערבית, he has not fulfilled his obligation. He supports this with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חיננא סבא said in the name of רב: Anyone who did not say 'אמת ויציב' in the morning and 'אמת ואמונה' at night has not fulfilled his obligation. As it says: 'To tell of Your kindness in the morning, and Your faithfulness at night.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about the wording of the ברכה after שמע. Each time of day has its own required opening words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The morning ברכה must open with אמת ויציב and the evening ברכה with אמת ואמונה. The פסוק links morning with kindness (חסד) and night with faithfulness (אמונה). The night version stresses trusting God even in the dark times.

keyTerms.meaning: 'True and firm', the opening of the morning ברכה after שמע
'True and faithful', the opening of the evening ברכה after שמע

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why our סידור has different openings after שמע: אמת ויציב in the morning and אמת ואמונה at night.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Ḥinnana Sava said in the name of Rav:
Anyone who did not say 'True and firm' in the morning,
and 'True and faithful' in the evening,
has not fulfilled his obligation,
as it is said: 'To tell of Your kindness in the morning'
'and Your faithfulness in the nights.'
phrases.notes: תהלים צב:ג

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, though it still concerns the wording of the ברכות of שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without אמת ויציב in the morning and אמת ואמונה at night, one is not יוצא. This is based on the פסוק about kindness in the morning and faithfulness at night.

steps.title: Bowing at ברוך and standing up at God's name
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חיננא סבא also says in the name of רב that when one bows in תפילה, he bows at the word ברוך and straightens up when he says God's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר חיננא סבא said in the name of רב: When a person prays and bows, he bows at 'ברוך'. When he straightens up, he straightens up at God's name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling from the same speaker. It tells us exactly when to bow down and when to stand up during שמונה עשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bow goes with the word ברוך ('Blessed'), and the person stands straight again by the time he says God's name. This sets the timing of the body's movement to match the words of the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Blessed', the opening word of a ברכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the common practice of bowing at ברוך and standing straight at God's name in שמונה עשרה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא [סָבָא] מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar Ḥinnana Sava said in the name of Rav:
One who prays, when he bows,
bows at 'Blessed',
and when he straightens up, he straightens up at God's name.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same speaker, continuing his series of statements about תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In תפילה, one bows at ברוך and straightens up at God's name.

steps.title: שמואל gives the פסוק behind רב's rule
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that רב's rule to straighten up at the שם comes from the פסוק ה׳ זוקף כפופים‎, 'ה׳ straightens the bent.'
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: What is רב's reason? As it is written: 'ה׳ straightens those who are bent over.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the source for the second half of רב's rule from step 28: why we stand up straight when we say God's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links God's name with straightening up those who are bent. So when a person reaches the שם, he straightens up. This reminds him that it is ה׳ who lifts up the bent.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who was a colleague of רב

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
What is Rav's reason?
phrases.notes: Rav's reason for standing up straight at God's name.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'ה׳ straightens the bent.'
phrases.notes: תהלים קמו:ח

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for רב's bowing rule in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that one straightens up at the שם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים: ה׳ זוקף כפופים, where ה׳'s name is tied to straightening the bent.

steps.title: A verse suggests humbling oneself before God's name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule with the פסוק 'מפני שמי נחת הוא', which praises the כהן for being humbled before God's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this from a פסוק: 'And before My name he was humbled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's explanation with a different פסוק. That פסוק seems to show that a person should be bent and humble at God's name, not straight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in מלאכי praises the כהן for being humbled in connection with God's name. If humility belongs at the שם, then we should be bowing at the שם, not standing up straight. That clashes with רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged; an objection is raised
He was humbled, broken, in awe

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'Before My name he was humbled.'
phrases.notes: מלאכי ב:ה, describing the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source and rule given in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule, backed by שמואל, that one straightens up at the שם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק links humility, meaning bowing, to God's name. That suggests one should be bent, not upright, at the שם.

steps.title: The verse says 'before' My name, not 'at' My name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק says מפני שמי, 'before My name,' not בשמי, 'at My name.' So the bowing comes before the שם, at ברוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'at My name'? It is written 'before My name.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב's rule by reading the exact words of the פסוק carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק said בשמי, it would mean bowing while saying the שם. It says מפני שמי, which means bowing before the שם arrives, at the word ברוך. So the פסוק actually fits רב: bow at ברוך, and straighten up at the שם.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? (a rhetorical question about the exact wording)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read מפני here as 'because of.' The answer depends on reading it as 'before,' meaning earlier in time than the שם.

phrases.english: Is it written 'at My name'?
'Before My name' is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי כְּתִיב בִּשְׁמִי מִפְּנֵי שְׁמִי כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means one bows at the moment of saying God's name.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means one bows before the name, at ברוך. At the name itself, one straightens up, as רב said.

steps.title: שמואל shares רב's teaching with רב's son
steps.stepSummary: שמואל calls חייא בר רב a 'son of Torah' and repeats his father רב's fine teaching: bow at ברוך, straighten up at the שם.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to חייא בר רב: Son of Torah, come and I will tell you a fine teaching that your father said. This is what your father said: When one bows, he bows at 'ברוך.' When he straightens up, he straightens up at the שם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. שמואל lovingly passes רב's bowing rule on to רב's son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new הלכה is added here. The story repeats the rule from step 28 word for word. It shows how much שמואל valued the teaching, calling it a מילתא מעלייתא, 'a fine saying.' It also shows the teaching being carried on to the next generation.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of תורה, a title of praise

steps.whatToRemember: In תפילה you bow at ברוך and straighten up at the שם. The source is ה׳ זוקף כפופים. The פסוק מפני שמי נחת הוא fits this, because the bowing comes before the name.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical way we bow in שמונה עשרה today.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב:
phrases.english: Shmuel said to Chiyya bar Rav:
Son of Torah,
come and I will tell you a fine teaching
that your father said.
This is what your father said:
When he bows, he bows at 'Baruch,'
when he straightens up, he straightens up at the Name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב בַּר אוֹרְיָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge is answered, the גמרא closes by restating רב's rule through שמואל's words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bow at ברוך; straighten up at the שם.
